The Oyo State Government has disbursed over ₦5.35 billion in compensation to 578 property owners affected by the First Segment of the Ibadan Circular Road Project, marking a major milestone in the implementation of one of the state’s most ambitious infrastructure projects and reaffirming Governor Seyi Makinde’s commitment to balancing development with the protection of citizens’ interests. Providing an update on the compensation exercise, the governor’s Executive Adviser on New Towns and Cities, Mrs Mofoluke Adebiyi, said the state government had recorded substantial progress in the payment process, with hundreds of affected property owners across both the Right of Way and Omission categories already receiving their approved compensation. This was contained in a statement issued by Makinde’s Special Adviser on Media, Sulaimon Olarenwaju, in Ibadan, the state capital, on Sunday. The statement explained that the first segment of the Ibadan Circular Road spans 32.2 kilometres, stretching from the Abiola Ajimobi Technical University axis on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway in the Oluyole Local Government Area, through Ona Ara LGA, and terminating at Badeku Junction on the Ibadan-Ife Expressway in Egbeda LGA. It read, “Under the right-of-way category, which comprises properties located within 75 metres on either side of the road median, a total of 674 structures were enumerated. Governor Makinde had approved a reduction of the initial setback from 150m to 75m in clustered and built-up areas following appeals and concerns expressed by residents across the affected local government areas. So far, 411 claimants have appeared before the screening committee and have been screened, while 378 claimants have successfully executed their Deeds of Indemnity, secured clearance and received their compensation payments. “The omission category consists of individuals who claimed that their properties were affected by the project without prior enumeration or compensation. In response, the state New Towns and Cities Development Authority, in collaboration with the Ministry of Lands, Housing and Urban Development and the Office of the Surveyor-General, conducted a fresh enumeration exercise, which identified 251 affected structures. “Following the exercise, Governor Makinde approved N1,813,954,100.00 as compensation for property owners under the omission category. Records show that 216 property owners have appeared before the Monitoring Team on Payment of Compensation Screening Committee, while 200 claimants who completed the required documentation and executed their Deeds of Indemnity have been cleared and paid a total of N1,493,784,700.00 as compensation.” The statement noted that “in total, 578 property owners across both categories have received compensation payments, representing significant progress in the administration’s determination to ensure that those affected by the project are adequately compensated.” Adebiyi noted that the compensation exercise remained ongoing and that the government is committed to ensuring that all eligible claimants who satisfy the stipulated requirements receive their payments. She explained that while 263 claimants in the ROW category and 35 claimants in the omission category have yet to appear before the committee, others are still expected to fulfil documentation requirements before final clearance. According to her, only 16 claimants experienced unsuccessful payment transactions due to discrepancies between the names submitted during screening and the bank account details provided, adding that efforts are ongoing to resolve the issues and facilitate payment. She reiterated that the compensation exercise has been conducted transparently, fairly and without favouritism, assuring all affected property owners that due process remains the guiding principle throughout the exercise. The government also reaffirmed its commitment to delivering transformative infrastructure while safeguarding the interests of affected residents. “The payment of over N5.35 billion in compensation reflects the administration’s resolve to ensure that development proceeds hand in hand with fairness, accountability and responsible governance,” the statement added. In late October 2026, The PUNCH reported that during a meeting with affected property owners along the road, Makinde approved N4.6bn as the first tranche of compensation for property owners affected by the ongoing project. According to a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media, Sulaimon Olarenwaju, the governor said the compensation would be paid directly into beneficiaries’ bank accounts, with disbursement beginning immediately.
